items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: My, my, my original God for the first time I was baptized was a Creole. He was black. Ijean de Plessis, which is French and black. That's when I was christened the first time.

ctx.x: You need all those four elements.

You need those four elements to make up a Creole. You're talking about French, Spanish, black, in conjunction with, of course, with whites and Indian, maybe four or five. This is the way I see it now. You take like Marie Laveau. Marie Laveau was a Creole. See, Marie Laveau was part French and black. Her daddy was a Frenchman. Her mother was part black and part Indian, the way it was told to me. So, she was a Creole. My, my, my original God for the first time I was baptized was a Creole. He was black. Ijean de…
don't want blacks to have that identity.
